start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:grow-the-one-tree with the seed 'New staff learn our order sheet faster from filled-in rows than from the how-to', owner task list record:calendar-task-list:example and pursuit pursuit:example-content, visibility public."

lists.label: Workflows
lists.holds: Every workflow is a branch of the tree: each row is one workflow (its id, title and job) and says when it fires on its own row (fires_when: a list of conditions, each the {fields, tree} tool:filter-rows-by-rules takes over one typed part of a seed). Adding a workflow, or installing a kit, adds a branch; no list of branches is kept.

values.title: Hand new staff the filled-in sheet
values.job: When someone new starts, give them three filled-in example rows of the order sheet before the how-to.

values.title: Turn a finding into a plan
values.job: Turn a research finding into a facts-first plan with its gaps named.

alike: a list of standard operating procedures with their triggers
a Zapier or Make list of automations

lists.label: Tree outputs
lists.holds: References only, one row per output of the one tree: the id of the row that holds it, the branch that made it, the seed, and the branches that reuse it. The output itself stays in its own list; nothing is copied here.
alike: a "where is this used" column in a content calendar

lists.label: Content pillars
lists.holds: What each pursuit's content is for: the few kinds of piece every video, post and picture must serve, with what the viewer gets and how often.

values.viewer_gets: A filled-in example they can copy into their own order sheet today.
values.never: A how-to with no filled-in example.

values.viewer_gets: What a real Saturday morning rush looks like, minute by minute.
values.never: Staged shots of an empty shop.

lists.label: Content formats
lists.holds: How each kind of piece is built (hook, beats, shots, text, sound, call to action), what it needs and the checks it must pass.

values.how_built: Hook reads the comment aloud; one beat shows the filled-in example; close names where to get it.
values.checks: The comment is shown word for word; captions on; vertical 9:16.

values.how_built: Open on the first customer; timelapse to the last tray; end on the count of loaves sold.
values.checks: No customer face without consent; the count matches the till.

alike: a swipe file of post templates

lists.label: Content pieces
lists.holds: Every piece to make for a pursuit: when it goes out, which pillar and format it serves and why, who does the next step, the script and the draft.

values.piece: How we train a new baker in one morning
values.why: A commenter asked how a new baker learns the morning bake in one shift.
values.script: You asked how a new baker learns the bake in a morning. We hand them yesterday's finished sheet, not a manual.

alike: an editorial board in Airtable or Trello

instructions: 1. Give each workflow you keep its conditions: on its row of your list of workflows (or a list you already keep for processes and their triggers, see pour) write fires_when, a list of {label, condition: {fields, tree}, made_by, state}. Workflows you install from the Workshop bring their own; a row of yours with only {recipe, fires_when} changes when an installed one fires.
2. Pour or make list:content-pillars, list:content-formats and list:content-pieces from their example rows, and make list:tree-outputs empty; the run writes it.

3. Say "Run workflow:grow-the-one-tree" with the seed (its words and where it came from), owner.task_list, owner.pursuit and visibility; the AI starts it with tool:start-a-recipe-run (row workflow:grow-the-one-tree).

4. Read the choose-branches answer: the parts the seed was split into and, for each, the workflows whose conditions kept it (tool:choose-the-workflows-that-fire), and any workflow the AI judged and gave a new condition on its row. Set a condition's state Off on its workflow's row if it should not fire for seeds like this.
5. Each output lands once in its owner list with a tree-outputs row naming the workflow that made it; later workflows read tree-outputs before they make anything.
6. Open the root task in the Calendar tasks table: the show step says which root task to open and how many children are Done.

worked_examples.title: One seed fires two workflows
worked_examples.ask: Grow the tree from this: new staff learn our order sheet faster from filled-in rows than from the how-to.

seed.words: New staff learn our order sheet faster from filled-in rows than from the how-to.

worked_examples.given: Among the person's workflows and the installed ones, workflow:turn-what-you-said-into-content fires when the seed is the person's own words and workflow:research-what-everyone-says when a seed makes a claim or names a subject (each condition on its own row).
worked_examples.hands_back: Parts: one claim ("filled-in rows teach faster than a how-to") and material for content (the person's own words). tool:choose-the-workflows-that-fire chose workflow:research-what-everyone-says for the claim and workflow:turn-what-you-said-into-content for the person's own words. The root task record:calendar-task:tree-hand-people-the-rows gets two child tasks, one per workflow, each naming the condition that chose it.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
